questions.q: What is the real purpose of a multi-signature wallet, per this lesson?
options: Requiring multiple owners to approve a transaction before it executes, reducing the risk of one bad actor draining funds
Making transactions execute instantly with no approval needed
Allowing anyone on the internet to withdraw funds freely
Replacing the need for a private key entirely
questions.explain: A multisig wallet's real purpose is shared control: no single owner can act alone, since a required number of approvals must be met first.

questions.q: What does the nested mapping `mapping(uint256 => mapping(address => bool)) public isConfirmed;` actually track?
options: For each transaction index, exactly which owner addresses have already confirmed it
The total balance of the wallet
A list of all transactions ever submitted
Which owners are allowed to deposit ETH
questions.explain: This nested mapping records, per transaction, a true/false confirmation status for every individual owner address.

questions.q: What does the `notExecuted` modifier actually check?
options: That the given transaction hasn't already been executed
That the caller is one of the contract's owners
That enough confirmations have been gathered
That the transaction index is a valid number
questions.explain: notExecuted requires that transactions[_txIndex].executed is false, preventing a transaction from running more than once.

questions.q: Why are all five real events (Deposit, SubmitTransaction, ConfirmTransaction, RevokeConfirmation, ExecuteTransaction) marked with `indexed` parameters?
options: So each event can later be searched and filtered on the blockchain by owner or transaction index
Indexed parameters make the events cost zero gas
It's required for events to compile at all
It hides the event from external tools like block explorers
questions.explain: Just like in the earlier Events lesson, indexed parameters let a block explorer or front end filter these logs by a specific owner or transaction index.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what makes this multisig contract's design not really a brand-new concept?
options: It combines the same real tools from earlier chapters — events, structs, nested mappings, and modifiers — at a larger scale
It uses an entirely new programming language
It has no real connection to anything covered earlier in the course
It avoids using modifiers or events entirely
questions.explain: Every piece of this contract's design — events, a struct, a nested mapping, and modifiers — is something already covered in Chapter 6, now combined into one larger, real application.
